instruction: Add an optional condition parameter to cachetools.cached, so the signature becomes cached(cache, key=hashkey, lock=None, condition=None, info=False). condition is an object like threading.Condition (a context manager with wait_for() and notify_all()). When it is given, concurrent calls for the same key don't all compute the value (no cache stampede): the others wait until the first has finished. The protocol, with the lock being lock if given and otherwise condition itself: acquire the lock, call condition.wait_for(predicate) until no other call is computing this key, then return the cached value if there is one, else mark the key as being computed and release; compute the value without holding the lock; acquire it again to store the value (a value too large for the cache is returned but not stored); and finally acquire it once more to unmark the key and call condition.notify_all(), even if computing failed. So a miss enters the lock three times and calls wait_for() and notify_all() once each; a hit enters it once and calls wait_for() once; cache_clear() and cache_info() (with info=True, same counts and values as today) enter it once each. Without condition, behavior is unchanged. The fourth positional argument used to be info: cached(cache, key, lock, True) must keep working as info=True but emit a DeprecationWarning. Make cachetools.func's decorators pass their threading.Condition as condition. Add tests.
